audit_findings.title: NGDV valuation depends on uncommitted follow-on orders recovering a large deferred-cost asset
audit_findings.magnitude: $796.9 million deferred contract costs and $75 million excess over profits on existing orders at 2026-06-30; broader OE impact unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Follow-on orders affect NGDV margins, deferred-cost amortization or impairment, and recurring Transport owner earnings.
audit_findings.evidence: The Company estimates that deferred contract costs exceed future profits on existing orders by approximately $ 135 million at December 31, 2025.
audit_findings.explanation: This is not yet a demonstrated valuation error: no impairment was recorded in the first half of 2026, and the disclosed recovery gap declined from $135 million to $75 million. The remaining $75 million equals about $1.20 per share or 1.1% of base equity value, which alone is not conclusion-changing. However, the filing still identifies dependence on an expected but uncommitted follow-on order, and the record does not quantify the larger recurring OE shortfall if that order does not arrive or has unfavorable pricing.
audit_findings.action: Obtain the NGDV order status, unit economics, remaining amortization schedule and management's probability-weighted recovery analysis; rerun each scenario with no follow-on order and with filed order pricing and margins.

audit_findings.title: The 2025 anchor predates a major recurring tariff step-up
audit_findings.magnitude: $165 million estimated 2026 pre-tax increase, equal to 35.0% of the $472.1 million anchor before offsets and tax; net OE impact unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Unrecovered tariff costs reduce 2026 and subsequent operating margins and owner earnings before scenario growth is applied.
audit_findings.evidence: The Company estimates tariffs will total approximately $200 million in 2026, which is an increase of approximately $165 million from 2025.
audit_findings.explanation: The anchor mismatch is demonstrated, although the net loss is not: 2026 first-half material costs increased $93 million, primarily from tariffs, while pricing improved $105 million across the company, and gross margin still fell 320 basis points. The filed $165 million annual cost step-up is large relative to anchor OE, so applying nonnegative growth directly to 2025 OE without a 2026 bridge can materially overstate value.
audit_findings.action: Build and verify a 2026 OE bridge using actual first-half tariffs, segment-level realized pricing, contractual recovery timing, volume effects, efficiencies and taxes; then rerun all scenarios from the resulting normalized 2026 OE.

audit_findings.title: Cash added to equity value may include customer-funded operating cash
audit_findings.magnitude: $403.6 million bridge addition, or $6.44 per share and 5.7% of base equity value; customer advances were $2,063.2 million at 2026-06-30
audit_findings.mechanism: Any cash required to fulfill customer-funded production or maintain operations should not be added as surplus cash in the equity bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: Customer advances include amounts received in advance of the completion of goods or services.
audit_findings.explanation: The filing does not establish that all $403.6 million is restricted, so a full overstatement is not demonstrated. It does establish $2.063 billion of customer advances and $2.289 billion of total contract liabilities, making the classification of all cash as distributable unsupported. Excluding the entire cash addition would reduce base value from $112.32 to about $105.88 per share and buy-below from $78.62 to about $74.11, a material bridge sensitivity.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile cash by entity and source to customer advances, restricted or foreign balances, near-term contract expenditures and minimum operating liquidity; rerun the bridge using only evidenced surplus cash.

audit_findings.title: Customer financing guarantees create claims not represented by the share denominator
audit_findings.magnitude: $126.4 million filed maximum credit-guarantee loss exposure, or $2.02 per share and 1.8% of base equity value; $12.0 million stand-ready and $4.5 million contingent exposures were recorded
audit_findings.mechanism: An unreserved expected guarantee loss would enter OE through credit-loss expense or reduce equity value as an incremental contingent liability; it does not alter the share count.
audit_findings.evidence: The Company is party to multiple agreements whereby at December 31, 2025, the Company guaranteed an aggregate of $ 559.0 million in indebtedness of customers.
audit_findings.explanation: The exposure increased from the 2025 amount, but even deducting the full filed maximum loss from equity—without credit for collateral or recorded obligations—would reduce base value only from $112.32 to about $110.30 per share. The actual incremental exposure is smaller because recorded obligations and collateral recoveries must be considered, so this finding is not presently large enough to alter the valuation conclusion.

audit_findings.title: A red-zone multi-employer pension plan may carry an unrecognized withdrawal claim
audit_findings.mechanism: Rehabilitation contributions would reduce recurring OE, while a withdrawal liability would be an equity-bridge claim ahead of common shareholders.
audit_findings.evidence: The plan-certified zone status (as defined by the Pension Protection Act of 2006) for the Boilermaker-Blacksmith National Pension Trust has been Red since January 2023.
audit_findings.explanation: The red-zone status and financial-improvement plan are demonstrated, but no Oshkosh withdrawal-liability estimate or plan-specific rehabilitation burden is supplied. Combined contributions to both multi-employer plans were only $3.1 million in 2025, about 0.7% of anchor OE, but that does not bound a withdrawal claim. The record therefore cannot establish whether the omitted burden is material.
audit_findings.action: Obtain the plan's latest funded status, rehabilitation schedule, Oshkosh contribution history and ERISA withdrawal-liability estimate; normalize OE for recurring increases or deduct a probability-weighted liability in the bridge.

audit_findings.title: The latest-year anchor may retain a nonrecurring tax benefit
audit_findings.magnitude: $17 million after-tax benefit; if fully embedded and perpetuated, computed base-value effect is approximately $238.8 million, $3.81 per share or 3.4% of base equity value
audit_findings.mechanism: A nonrecurring tax benefit retained in anchor OE is multiplied through forecast OE and terminal value.
audit_findings.evidence: The effective tax rate in 2025 included net discrete tax benefits of $17 million primarily related to the release of uncertain tax positions on the resolution of a multi-year federal income tax audit.
audit_findings.explanation: Retention in the $472.1 million anchor is not demonstrated and must be traced. Even under the conservative assumption that the entire $17 million was retained and perpetuated, removing it would reduce base value from $112.32 to about $108.51 per share and buy-below from $78.62 to about $75.95. That does not change the valuation conclusion at the supplied $157.08 market price.
audit_findings.action: Trace the $17 million benefit through the OE worksheet; if retained, remove it from anchor OE and rerun the scenarios, while separately normalizing any 2026 discrete tax benefits.
